title: Pragmatic Engineer canvass: ~20 engineering leaders report shrinking teams, including a 10,000-developer agriculture firm moving from six-to-ten to three-to-four
summary: Gergely Orosz reported on 24 February 2026 that around 20 engineering leaders he spoke with — many at large enterprises, some at small startups — said their engineering teams are shrinking. One account carries numbers and a described organisation: a Head of Engineering at a 200-year-old agriculture company with more than 10,000 developers said 'we are already seeing the end of two-pizza teams (6-10 people) thanks to AI. Our teams are slowly but surely becoming one-pizza teams (3-4 people) across the business.' The value of that particular account is where it comes from: a traditional physical-goods manufacturer, not a software startup and not a venture portfolio company, which is the population the forerunner-only reading of this change predicts would be last to move. The canvass itself is informal — leaders self-selected into two invitation-based industry events, roughly 500 attendees at the Pragmatic Summit and 50 at a Future of Software Development workshop — and only the one account is quantified; the other nineteen are summarised in a single sentence with no companies, sizes or figures attached.
sampleSize: around 20 engineering leaders spoken with, drawn from two invitation-based industry events (Pragmatic Summit, ~500 attendees; Future of Software Development workshop, ~50 attendees); one account quantified
leadTimeEstimate: ~12-18 months ahead of population-level benchmark confirmation
whyItMatters: The one quantified account is from a 200-year-old agriculture manufacturer with 10,000-plus developers. If the shrinking-team pattern were confined to well-funded startups, this is precisely where it should not be appearing.
Six-to-ten down to three-to-four is a halving of the delivery unit stated as an ongoing programme rather than a target, which is a different kind of claim from a reorg announcement.
Nineteen of the twenty accounts carry no numbers. Leaders reading 'teams are shrinking' as an established industry fact should know how thin the quantified base underneath that sentence is.
recommendedActions: Ask peers reporting smaller teams for the two numbers — before and after — rather than accepting the direction of travel. This item exists because almost nobody in the canvass supplied them.
risksAndCaveats: The canvass is informal and self-selected: leaders who attend AI-focused industry events are not a representative sample of engineering organisations.
Only one of roughly twenty accounts is quantified, and the company is described rather than named, so the figure cannot be independently checked.
'Team' is not defined in the source. The 6-10 and 3-4 figures are presented as two-pizza and one-pizza teams, which is a norm rather than a measured unit.
The account states a transition in progress ('slowly but surely becoming'), not a completed measurement of current team sizes.
